body.heading: The idea underneath
paragraphs: The original practice, popularised by Julia Cameron, is simple: write three pages of whatever is in your head, first thing, without stopping or rereading. The point is to clear mental clutter onto paper.
Three pages is a lot, though, and strict rules make many people quit by day four. The useful core is smaller: write briefly, early, and without performing for an audience.

body.heading: Shrink it to fit your life
paragraphs: Try one page, or ten minutes, whichever comes first. Write in a cheap notebook so the paper never feels precious. Complaints, lists, half-dreams and grocery items all count.
Skip days without guilt and never reread the same week you wrote. You are sweeping the path, not building a monument, and a swept path is easier to walk on.

body.heading: A note on sources
paragraphs: If you want the original method in full, Cameron's book 'The Artist's Way' describes it in detail. The gentle version here is an adaptation, not a replacement.
Adapt freely. The habit belongs to you once it fits your mornings, and a smaller version kept for a year will do more than the strict version abandoned in a week.

takeaway: One unpolished page in the morning can clear the desk inside your head.
